answer.rationale: The competitor price cut creates strong pull toward promotional_pricing, but that is exactly the lever the record warns against: memory_73 says targeted discounting buys acquisition and revenue while materially damaging 30-day retention, and explicitly says do not generalize it. Under a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, matching a deeper price cut trades durable revenue for a short reprieve, and any win it books would likely be re-consolidated into memory as a general-purpose growth tactic — a contamination risk I am flagging rather than accepting. The strongest evidence I hold that is both retention-positive and directly relevant to SMB self-serve is exp_86 / memory_86: shortened onboarding, completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, conclusion confirmed. Faster time-to-value is a defensible answer to price pressure because it raises perceived value rather than lowering price. I note the adjacent evidence is weaker than it looks: exp_31 (signup simplification) is confirmed only on SMB, was not replicated on other segments, and carries retention -1%, so I am leaning on the onboarding-shortening result, not conflating the two under one 'simplification' label. Scale is standard_experiment, not broad rollout: exp_86 is a single confirmed result and was never tested under an active competitive price shock, so its lift may not hold against churn driven by price rather than friction. Verification budget is spent, so I am carrying that gap forward as stated uncertainty rather than resolving it. Referral incentive (memory_57) is clean but is evidenced on established customers, not the price-pressured SMB base, and activation messaging (memory_91) is a plausible additive complement; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a different segment than the one churning. Recommend flagging to leadership that if a pricing response is judged unavoidable, it should be a small guarded test scoped to the price-sensitive SMB cohort with retention as a gating metric, and its result must not be recorded as a general growth finding.
